title: Maximising Savings: 9 Reinvestment Options for Capital Gains Tax Exemption
description: Selling capital assets like property, land, shares, or mutual funds can lead to capital gains tax. The Income-tax Act, 1961, offers exemptions if these gains .

faq.q: What is a long-term capital gain?
faq.a: A long-term capital gain arises from the sale of a capital asset held for more than a specified period (e.g., 24 months for immovable property, 12 months for shares/mutual funds).

faq.q: Can I claim exemption under Section 54 if I buy multiple houses?
faq.a: Generally, Section 54 exemption is available for the purchase or construction of one residential house property. However, for sales made on or after April 1, 2020, an exemption can be claimed for two residential house properties if the capital gain does not exceed ₹2 crore. This benefit can be availed only once in a lifetime.

faq.q: Are NRIs eligible for these capital gains exemptions?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally eligible for capital gains exemptions under various sections, provided they meet all the conditions specified in the Income-tax Act, including reinvestment within India.

faq.q: What happens if I sell the new asset before the lock-in period?
faq.a: If you sell the new asset (e.g., house, bonds) before the specified lock-in period, the capital gains exemption previously claimed may be revoked, and the exempted amount could become taxable in the year of sale.

faq.q: Is there a maximum limit for capital gains exemption?
faq.a: While some sections like 54EC and 54EE have a maximum investment limit of ₹50 lakh per financial year, other sections like 54 and 54F generally allow exemption up to the amount of capital gains or the cost of the new asset, without an upper monetary limit on the gain itself.

faq.q: What is the due date for depositing funds into the Capital Gains Account Scheme?
faq.a: The amount must be deposited into the Capital Gains Account Scheme before the due date for filing your income tax return for the assessment year in which the transfer took place.

faq.q: Do I need to report the reinvestment in my income tax return?
faq.a: Yes, you must report the capital gains and the reinvestment made to claim exemption in your Income Tax Return (ITR) form, typically ITR-2 or ITR-3.
